markets: Stores and online sales in the United States and Canada.
rationale: Premium US retailer; F1 could support US luxury audiences, but it is North America only and rarely sponsors sport.
changed: Taken private by the Nordstrom family and El Puerto de Liverpool in 2025

name: Chanel
desc: Luxury fashion house founded in 1910 selling couture, ready-to-wear, leather goods, fragrance, make-up and jewellery, owned by the Wertheimer family.
markets: Boutiques and wholesale across Europe, the Americas, Asia and the Middle East.
rationale: Elite global brand, but it historically avoids sponsorship, so partnership with F1 is unlikely despite the audience fit.

name: Takko Fashion
desc: German value fashion retailer from Telgte operating about 1,800 stores across Europe selling low-priced clothing for the family.
markets: Stores across Germany and other European countries; no verified expansion beyond Europe.
rationale: Discount fashion chain with price-led marketing and limited budget; weak F1 fit.

name: BVI Medical
desc: Maker of ophthalmic surgical devices including cataract and retinal instruments, intraocular lenses and glaucoma implants sold to surgeons and hospitals.
markets: Products sold to surgeons and hospitals in North America, Europe, Asia and other regions.
rationale: B2B surgical device maker without consumer marketing or sponsorship culture; weak F1 fit.

name: Allbirds
desc: San Francisco footwear and apparel brand known for Wool Runner and Tree Runner sneakers made from merino wool and eucalyptus.
markets: Sold online and in stores in the United States, Europe and Asia, with shrinking store footprint.
rationale: Sustainability-led brand with limited budget; F1's sustainability agenda is relevant but financial pressure limits fit.

name: OVS
desc: Italian fashion retailer with about 1,000 OVS, OVS Kids and Upim stores selling affordable clothing for men, women and children.
markets: Stores mainly in Italy, with some franchise sales abroad; no verified large expansion plans.
rationale: Italian mass-market brand; F1 is plausible for Italian fan reach but marketing budget is modest.

name: New Era Cap
desc: Buffalo headwear company founded in 1920, known for the 59FIFTY fitted cap and as Major League Baseball cap supplier.
markets: Sells caps and apparel through retailers, own stores and online across the Americas, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Existing F1 partner; strong brand-led fit with youth audiences and licensed merchandise.
f1: New Era is a current F1 partner

name: CaratLane
desc: Indian omnichannel jewellery brand founded in 2008 selling diamond, gold and gemstone jewellery through stores and online.
markets: Stores and online sales in India; majority owned by Titan Company since 2023.
rationale: Marketing-led Indian jewellery brand; F1 gives limited reach beyond a small premium Indian audience.
changed: Majority acquired by Titan Company in 2023

name: Lands' End
desc: US apparel and home goods retailer selling casual clothing, outerwear, swimwear and school uniforms through its website, catalogues and stores.
markets: Sales in the United States with websites serving the UK, Germany and Japan.
rationale: Mature mail-order and online apparel brand with limited marketing budget; F1 fit is weak.

name: Moda Operandi
desc: New York luxury fashion e-commerce platform using a trunk-show and pre-order model to sell designer clothing, shoes and bags.
markets: Ships to customers in the United States and many other countries.
rationale: Luxury online platform with affluent clients; F1 hospitality could suit VIP clients, but its scale is modest.

name: Ermenegildo Zegna Group
desc: Italian luxury group founded in 1910 making menswear under Zegna and Thom Browne, with the Tom Ford Fashion licence.
markets: Own stores, wholesale and e-commerce across Europe, the Americas and Asia, including a large China business.
rationale: Global luxury menswear brand with affluent customers; F1 paddock hospitality and tailoring suits fit its premium positioning.

name: Canada Goose
desc: Toronto luxury outdoor apparel maker famous for down-filled parkas, selling through own stores, e-commerce and wholesale in over 50 countries.
markets: Stores and wholesale across North America, Europe and Asia, with strong China growth.
rationale: Premium brand seeking international growth; F1 can help build visibility and hospitality beyond winter markets.

name: Fielmann
desc: German optician founded in 1972, Europe's largest by volume, selling glasses, contact lenses and hearing aids in about 1,000 stores.
markets: Stores in Germany, Austria, Switzerland and other European countries.
rationale: Large European consumer retailer with heavy advertising; F1 fit is plausible but eyewear rivals already sponsor.

name: PVH Corp
desc: US apparel group owning Calvin Klein and Tommy Hilfiger, selling clothing, underwear, footwear and accessories globally through stores and online.
markets: Stores and wholesale across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Existing F1 link through Tommy Hilfiger; Calvin Klein adds further brand potential for expansion.
f1: Owns Tommy Hilfiger, a current F1 partner

name: The Children's Place
desc: US children's apparel retailer selling kids' clothing through roughly 500 stores and online in North America.
markets: Stores in the United States and Canada, plus international franchise partners.
rationale: North American children's chain under financial pressure with a limited marketing budget; weak F1 fit.

name: Smart Fabric
desc: Shenzhen company providing internet-enabled solutions and software for the textile industry, according to Crunchbase.
markets: Presumably serves Chinese textile makers; scale, customers and international plans are not known to us.
rationale: Niche Chinese B2B textile software provider with no known marketing profile or international activity; weak F1 fit.

name: Galeria
desc: German department store chain, formerly Galeria Karstadt Kaufhof, selling fashion, beauty and household goods through about 80 stores.
markets: Stores in Germany only; repeated insolvencies have reduced its footprint.
rationale: Distressed domestic retailer with no international business and repeated insolvencies; weak F1 fit.
changed: Filed for insolvency in 2020, 2022 and 2024

name: Groupe Dynamite
desc: Canadian fashion retail group owning Dynamite and Garage apparel brands, selling clothing to young women through mall stores and online.
markets: Stores and online sales in Canada, the United States and Europe.
rationale: Youth-focused brand with growth plans in the US; F1 could reach its young female audience, though budgets are modest.

name: GIVA
desc: Indian online jewellery brand selling silver jewellery to young women, backed by Fireside Ventures.
markets: Customers in India through its website and stores; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Young Indian online jewellery brand with limited scale and no international business; F1 fit is weak.

name: Vestis
desc: US uniform and workplace supplies rental firm serving 300,000 business customers in the US and Canada with uniforms and mats.
markets: Customers across the United States and Canada; spun off from Aramark in 2023.
rationale: B2B service provider; F1 could host business customers, but it has no consumer brand focus.
changed: Spun off from Aramark in 2023

name: Farfetch
desc: London-based online luxury fashion marketplace connecting boutiques and brands with consumers in about 190 countries.
markets: Customers in about 190 countries, with operations across Europe, the Americas and Asia.
rationale: Global luxury platform with affluent users; F1 hospitality fits designer partners, though finances were stressed before the sale.
changed: Acquired by Coupang in 2024

name: Secoo
desc: Chinese online and offline luxury retailer selling fashion, watches, jewellery and lifestyle goods through an app, website and physical stores.
markets: Customers in China through its app and stores; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Chinese luxury platform with uncertain current status and no known international operations; weak F1 fit.

name: Tanger
desc: US real estate investment trust owning and operating open-air outlet shopping centres leased to retail brands.
markets: About 30 properties in the United States and Canada.
rationale: Property owner with tenant brands; F1 hospitality could help leasing relationships, but the fit is weak.

name: Brands for Less
desc: Dubai online and offline fashion discount retailer selling clothing, shoes, bags and home items from international brands at reduced prices.
markets: Stores and online sales across the Middle East; expansion plans are not confirmed.
rationale: Gulf consumer retailer; Abu Dhabi, Qatar and Saudi Grand Prix visibility could suit it, but it has no sponsorship record.

name: Synsam Group
desc: Stockholm-based Nordic optical retailer operating about 600 eyewear and optician stores in Sweden, Norway, Finland and Denmark.
markets: Stores in Sweden, Norway, Finland and Denmark; no verified expansion plans outside the Nordic region.
rationale: Regional optician chain; F1 fit is weak because it has no international business and rivals already sponsor.

name: Tradeinn
desc: Spanish e-commerce group running about 11 specialist online stores for sports and outdoor gear including Diveinn, Bikeinn and Runnerinn.
markets: Online sales from Spain across Europe and further markets; expansion plans are not confirmed.
rationale: Online sports retailer with niche audiences; F1 fit is modest, mainly through cycling and sports-fan communities.

name: SRTX
desc: Montreal company developing advanced textiles and fibres for fashion, sportswear and industrial uses, according to Crunchbase.
markets: Likely sells to apparel and industrial customers; international activity and expansion plans are unknown to us.
rationale: B2B materials developer with little brand profile; F1 could showcase fibre technology but fit is weak.

name: Dolce & Gabbana
desc: Italian luxury fashion house founded in 1985 selling ready-to-wear, accessories, eyewear, fragrance, beauty and jewellery worldwide.
markets: Boutiques and wholesale across Europe, the Americas, Asia and the Middle East.
rationale: Global luxury brand with affluent customers; F1 offers premium visibility, hospitality and Italian heritage alignment.

name: LPP
desc: Polish fashion retail group owning Reserved, Cropp, House, Mohito and Sinsay, selling through thousands of stores and online.
markets: Stores and online sales in Poland, Central and Eastern Europe and other European markets.
rationale: Large European fashion group with growth plans; F1 could help brand reach in Europe, though it has little sponsorship history.

name: Purple Style Labs
desc: Indian fashion retail company behind Pernia's Pop-Up Shop, a platform selling Indian designer wear for women, men and children.
markets: Customers mainly in India, with online shipping abroad; international expansion plans are not confirmed.
rationale: Indian luxury fashion platform; F1 audience is small in its market, so fit is weak.

name: Reformation
desc: US sustainable women's fashion brand selling dresses, tops, denim and shoes through its own stores and website.
markets: Stores and online sales in the United States, with shipping to other countries; expansion plans are not confirmed.
rationale: Sustainability-led consumer brand with young female customers; F1's sustainability agenda may fit, but it has no sponsorship record.

name: Burlington Stores
desc: US off-price retailer of apparel, shoes, home goods and accessories, formerly Burlington Coat Factory, operating over 1,000 stores.
markets: Stores in the United States and Puerto Rico only.
rationale: Domestic discount chain with little sponsorship culture and no international business; weak F1 fit.
